rows.proposedComment: Thanks for the report and the follow-up details. This failure path was fixed by https://github.com/microsoft/vscode-eslint/commit/d8214448aa1ba338c84184239bfee66cea24fbaa: errors from `fs.realpathSync.native` are now caught, and the server continues with the original file path rather than dropping linting with an unhandled `ENOENT`. rows.verifyEvidence: The report's stack trace is an unhandled ENOENT thrown by fs.realpathSync.native in getFileSystemPath; the diff wraps exactly that call in try/catch, so linting proceeds instead of failing silently.

rows.title: Reporting errors from node_module and no way to suppress/disable (also ignores .eslintignore)`
rows.proposedComment: Thanks for the detailed reproduction. ESLint confirmed this legacy-config ordering problem in https://github.com/eslint/eslint/issues/14686: it can load a dependency's `eslintConfig` before determining that the file is ignored. That upstream change was declined, and `eslint.onIgnoredFiles` does not suppress this case because the configuration error happens before the ignore result is available. Keeping this open to track whether the extension should avoid validating ignored `node_modules` documents before invoking ESLint.

rows.title: Prefer to use node from environment
Feature Request: enable the "eslint.format.enable" setting by default.
rows.proposedComment:
Thanks for the suggestion. `eslint.format.enable` is intentionally opt-in because VS Code can use different formatting providers, including TypeScript and Prettier. Enabling ESLint's formatter for everyone would change behavior for users who deliberately rely on another provider and would therefore be a breaking default change.

The Azure Pipelines extension is unrelated here; “formatting pipeline” refers to VS Code's formatting-provider flow. To use ESLint for formatting, enable `eslint.format.enable` and configure `dbaeumer.vscode-eslint` as `editor.defaultFormatter` for the relevant languages. For automatic ESLint fixes on save, `editor.codeActionsOnSave` with `source.fixAll.eslint` generally provides better control.

rows.title: A change to eslint.debug requires VSCode restart if the ESLint server was already running
rows.proposedComment: Thanks for the report and confirmation. The current client code reads `eslint.debug` when the language client is created and stores the resulting server environment in its launch options. `ESLint: Restart ESLint Server` restarts that existing client, so it reuses the old environment instead of recomputing `DEBUG`; a full VS Code restart creates a new client and explains why that works. This should remain open as a client restart bug. The broader report about `eslint.config.js` changes and the output channel may have a separate cause and still needs the requested reproduction repository.

rows.proposedComment: Thanks for clarifying the distinction from Yarn Plug'n'Play. Current main still uses the resolved parser path when probing legacy configurations, and the Yarn v4 pnpm-linker path in the reproduction does not match the `@typescript-eslint/parser` expression. Flat config on ESLint 9 bypasses that parser-path check, so could you confirm whether the reproduction still fails with ESLint 9 and whether it uses flat config or a legacy `.eslintrc`? The explicit `eslint.validate` entries remain a workaround, but they do not address automatic probing for this installation layout.

rows.title: Feature request: Provide a way to control files fixed during onCodeActionsSave (e.g., ignorePatterns)
rows.proposedComment: Thanks for the request. This is now supported through `eslint.codeActionsOnSave.options`, which was added in extension 3.0.16. That setting is passed as a separate ESLint options object when fixes are computed on save, so you can use `ignorePatterns` there to exclude files from fix-on-save without excluding them from normal validation. You can also use `overrideConfigFile` if maintaining a dedicated save-time ESLint configuration is a better fit. The implementation is in https://github.com/microsoft/vscode-eslint/commit/6f8769b072debf9ac124b55893dbc19e1bf8795d. The fix shipped in release/3.0.16.
rows.verifyEvidence: The commit adds `eslint.codeActionsOnSave.options`, spreading an arbitrary ESLint class options object (including ignorePatterns/ignorePath) into the save-time fix run, delivering the requested per-save ignore control generically.

rows.proposedComment: Thanks for the detailed reproduction and follow-up context. typescript-eslint 8.3.0 added a useful reload fallback in https://github.com/typescript-eslint/typescript-eslint/pull/9853, but that change was explicitly limited to the file-not-found case, and the later reports here show remaining gaps. The extension currently watches ESLint configuration files rather than arbitrary source-file changes, and `ESLint: Revalidate` does not provide the project service with incremental file-system updates. I think this should remain open for a coordinated watcher or invalidation API that lets typescript-eslint update its long-lived project service without forcing a full ESLint restart. https://github.com/microsoft/vscode-eslint/issues/1774 is related broader work around stale cross-file information, but it does not necessarily cover registering newly created files with the project service.

respect estlint-suppressions.json
rows.proposedComment: Thanks for the report and discussion. Bulk-suppression support has now shipped in stable version 3.0.34. With ESLint 10.1 or newer, use `eslint.bulkSuppression.enable` to apply the suppression file and surface suppressed violations at the severity selected by `eslint.bulkSuppression.severity`; `eslint.bulkSuppression.location` supports a non-default file path. If suppressed violations should be hidden entirely, `eslint.options` can pass `applySuppressions: true` without enabling their diagnostic display. The implementation landed in https://github.com/microsoft/vscode-eslint/commit/9d33f02b2ddaadc55f7f30dfd2338ccca12dc798. The fix shipped in release/3.0.34.
rows.verifyEvidence: Suppressions are only applied when the opt-in eslint.bulkSuppression.enable setting is on, and then re-emitted as info diagnostics; by default eslint-suppressions.json is still ignored entirely, so violations aren't suppressed.

rows.title: Loading flat config from the node_modules fails
Measure rule performance through VSCode ESLint
rows.proposedComment: Thanks for the detailed proposal. The first approach is the right integration point: `eslint.options` is already passed to the ESLint constructor, so `{ "stats": true }` can enable collection through ESLint's Node.js API. The missing piece is that the server currently consumes diagnostics and fixes from each lint result but does not read or present its `stats` property. Keeping this open to add an opt-in representation in the ESLint output channel; a custom executable wrapper should not be necessary.

rows.title: FEAT: Use ESLint extension without auto run
rows.proposedComment: Thanks for clarifying the request. `eslint.rules.customizations` can hide selected diagnostics, but it does not stop ESLint from running, and `eslint.run` currently only supports `onType` or `onSave`. Keeping this open as a feature request to decouple formatter registration from automatic validation, so `eslint.format.enable` can remain available for manual formatting without background diagnostics.

rows.title: Server side workingDirectory.mode auto detection is incomplete
multithreaded/--concurrency support?
rows.proposedComment: Thanks for the additional GraphQL ESLint context. The extension currently validates each document by passing its current editor contents to ESLint's `lintText`, while ESLint's concurrency support gains parallelism by processing multiple input files. Although `eslint.options` can forward the `concurrency` constructor option, that alone does not make a one-document `lintText` operation parallel. Keeping this open to investigate whether compatible validation requests can be batched without losing unsaved content or per-document configuration.

rows.title: Extension should report config file errors
rows.proposedComment: Thanks for the report. Invalid ESLint configurations are reported through VS Code's language status indicator for the affected document, with the detailed error available in the `ESLint` output channel. The same request was reviewed in https://github.com/microsoft/vscode-eslint/issues/1402#issuecomment-3645936662, where that presentation was confirmed as the recommended VS Code behavior. Reporting a precise diagnostic on `eslint.config.mjs` would also require ESLint to provide a reliable source location, which runtime configuration errors generally do not include.

rows.title: Request: add quick-fix action for adding same-line disables, i.e. `// eslint-disable-line`
rows.proposedComment: Thanks for the clarification. The `eslint.codeAction.disableRuleComment.location` setting is a useful workaround, but it selects one comment location for the resource; it does not expose same-line and separate-line choices at the same time. This issue should remain open for that per-invocation quick-fix choice, separately from https://github.com/microsoft/vscode-eslint/issues/1074, which requests automatic JSX/TSX context detection.

rows.title: /* eslint-disable-next-line no-unused-vars */  will disappear when save
rows.proposedComment:
Thanks for providing the project. Its recommended TypeScript configuration disables the core `no-unused-vars` rule and enables `@typescript-eslint/no-unused-vars` instead. That makes `/* eslint-disable-next-line no-unused-vars */` an unused directive, so ESLint removes it when fix-on-save runs. Please target the active plugin rule instead:

```ts
/* eslint-disable-next-line @typescript-eslint/no-unused-vars */
const value = 1
```

The extension is applying the fix produced by the workspace's ESLint installation here.

rows.title: docs: Document for `eslint.lintTask.command` is missing
ESLint plugin breaks when using `eslint-plugin-react-hooks`
rows.proposedComment: Thanks for the additional details. The key distinction is that normal per-file validation works; this happens in `eslint: lint whole folder`. That task uses VS Code's built-in `$eslint-stylish` problem matcher, and the multiline messages emitted by these rules interrupt its single-line diagnostic pattern, so only part of the task output reaches the Problems view and the rule code can be lost. This looks related to the VS Code task problem-matcher limitation tracked at https://github.com/microsoft/vscode/issues/9635, although this ESLint-specific integration still needs to remain tracked here.

rows.title: Eslint client couldn't create connection to server after installing new VS Code version
rows.proposedComment: Thanks for the report. I couldn't reproduce this, so could you confirm whether it still happens with the current VS Code and ESLint extension releases? If it does, please also share whether `eslint.runtime` or `eslint.execArgv` is configured and include the Extension Host log from the failed startup. The existing trace shows the IPC child process failing before the ESLint server starts, so those details will help determine whether this is in the extension's launch configuration or the underlying VS Code/language-client runtime.

rows.title: ESLint version 10.0.3 only supports flat configs. Setting is ignored
rows.proposedComment: Thanks for the report and investigation. This was a spurious message caused by the default value of `eslint.experimental.useFlatConfig` being sent as though it had been explicitly configured. It was fixed by https://github.com/microsoft/vscode-eslint/pull/2172 in https://github.com/microsoft/vscode-eslint/commit/5a2809ce452e41c84747b86a0334734e87e9c87b. The fix first shipped in pre-release 3.0.25 and is included in stable release 3.0.34. The fix shipped in release/3.0.34.
rows.verifyEvidence: The client previously always sent experimental.useFlatConfig defaulting to false, triggering the server's `=== false` warning branch; the diff sends it undefined when unset and warns only on explicit settings.

Lint whole folder task ignores workingDirectories setting
rows.proposedComment: Thanks for the report and the follow-up work. This remains a real gap on current `main`: `client/src/tasks.ts` still contributes one lint task rooted at the workspace folder and does not read `eslint.workingDirectories`. The two proposed implementations in https://github.com/microsoft/vscode-eslint/pull/635 and https://github.com/microsoft/vscode-eslint/pull/1861 were not merged; the latter also exposed portability and error-handling problems with chaining directory commands in a shell. The preferred direction from the discussion is one task per applicable working directory, with each task running ESLint using that directory as its `cwd`, rather than one shell command that chains every directory.

rows.title: Quick Fix for CRLF to LF does not work
Support specifying the shell to use for Lint task to avoid problems with bash under Windows.
rows.proposedComment: Thanks for the report and the follow-up investigation. VS Code's task customization now provides the needed configuration directly: add an `eslint` task entry to `.vscode/tasks.json` and set `options.shell`, as shown in https://github.com/microsoft/vscode-eslint/issues/795#issuecomment-1152778571. For Git Bash on Windows, selecting `cmd.exe` with `args: ["/d", "/c"]` lets the contributed lint task execute the discovered `.cmd` binary without using the integrated terminal's default shell. Since the shell can be selected through the standard task configuration, no additional ESLint setting is needed.
